goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:24: The default 50-member limit makes remaining members inaccessible on the public group members page because it lacks pagination controls or further-page loading.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the groups_controller.rb members action now returns paginated results with limit/offset parameters. The frontend code in group-members.js.es6 shows setupController calls model.findMembers() but the template group/members.hbs only iterates over members without any pagination controls visible in the diff. However, examining the admin side, there ARE pagination controls added (previous/next actions, currentPage/totalPages computed properties). The public group members page (discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) only changes from 'model' to 'members' in the each loop but doesn't add pagination controls. The controller in group-members.js.es6 just calls model.findMembers() without setting up pagination. So users viewing a public group with >50 members would only see the first 50 with no way to see more. This is a real functional limitation introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34: Existing PATCH /admin/groups/:id requests using changes.add or changes.delete silently skip membership changes while returning success.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the old code had an `update` method that checked `if request.patch?` and called `update_patch(group)` which handled `params[:changes]` with `add` and `delete` arrays for incremental membership changes. The new code completely removes this PATCH handling - the new `update` method only handles name, alias_level, and visible properties. If existing clients send PATCH requests with `changes.add` or `changes.delete`, the new `update` method will simply ignore those parameters and return success_json, silently not performing the membership changes. This is a real backward compatibility/API breaking change where the server returns success but doesn't actually do what was requested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34: Existing PATCH requests that omit visible set it to false, unintentionally hiding the group.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the update method in groups_controller.rb, line 34 shows `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. This means if a PATCH/PUT request doesn't include the 'visible' parameter, params[:visible] will be nil, and `nil == "true"` evaluates to false, so visible will be set to false. This is a real bug - any update request that doesn't explicitly pass visible=true will unintentionally hide the group. The old code had `group.visible = payload[:visible] == "true"` which had the same issue, but the finding is about the current code behavior which is indeed problematic for partial updates.
